verdict.rationale: dltHub documents its own scheduling for deployed pipelines, letting you schedule, refresh, backfill and observe runs through a decorator-based Python API. That suggests per-pipeline schedule control, but the evidence gives no detail on granularity or trigger types. Running under Airflow or GitHub Actions is a host-platform workaround and earns no credit. missing for 10: documented cron-expression support, sub-hour schedule intervals, explicit manual/on-demand trigger, per-pipeline frequency configuration details, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a data engineer, I control sync frequency per pipeline — from sub-hour schedules to cron expressions and manual triggers
